name: Question 3
worked_solution:
Here, $B$ is a $1\times 3$ matrix and $C$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix. 

There are $3$ columns in $B$ and $3$ rows in $C,$ so $B$ and $C$ are conformable for multiplication:

$$
{B}_{1\times \boxed{\text{3}}}{\cdot }_{✓}{C}_{\boxed{\text{3}}\times 2}={BC}_{1\times 2}
$$

Let's compute $BC,$ one element at a time:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-10 & ∗\end{aligned}], &  & \,-10=(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 3+(-2)\cdot 5 \\  & [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \\ 5 & 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-10 & -14\end{aligned}], &  & \,-14=(-3)\cdot 2+1\cdot 4+(-2)\cdot 6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$BC=[\begin{aligned}-10 & -14\end{aligned}].$

Question 3
?

Find BC, if B=[−31−2] and C=[123456].

a
[−10−14]
b
[−114]
c
[−1−7]
d
[10−1]
e
[514]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, B is a 1×3 matrix and C is a 3×2 matrix.

There are 3 columns in B and 3 rows in C, so B and C are conformable for multiplication:

B1×3⋅✓C3×2=BC1×2

Let's compute BC, one element at a time:

[−31−2][123456]=[−10∗],−10=(−3)⋅1+1⋅3+(−2)⋅5[−31−2][123456]=[−10−14],−14=(−3)⋅2+1⋅4+(−2)⋅6

Therefore, BC=[−10−14].
